blocks.text: Ask me where to drink in Bondi and I'll answer before you finish the question: start beachfront with a sundowner, then wander inland as the night warms up. After years of living a few streets back from the sand, these are the ten bars I actually send friends to — a mix of ocean-view balconies, a proper microbrewery, a couple of cosy locals' corners and one or two that keep going long after the surf lights switch off.

items.label: Best for views
items.value: Icebergs, North Bondi RSL, Hotel Ravesis

items.label: Getting here
items.value: Bus to Bondi Beach, or the 333 from the city

blocks.text: My beachfront big-hitters
1. Hotel Ravesis

You can't miss the flamingo-pink corner where Hall Street meets Campbell Parade. Ravesis is the one I aim for when I want the whole spectrum in a single building — an easy schooner or a glass of rosé on the terrace early, then upstairs as the DJs get going and it tips into the small hours. Grab a spot on the front terrace for that classic wide-open view over the promenade to the water.
2. Icebergs (the Bondi Bar balcony)

For the postcard, nothing beats the balcony bar at Icebergs, perched above the famous ocean pool at the south end. It's a dress-up-a-little kind of place and the drinks are priced for the view, but a negroni at golden hour looking down the length of the beach is one of those genuinely Sydney moments. It's popular and often booked, so check the Icebergs website and reserve ahead if you want a table.
3. North Bondi RSL

My honest tip for the best value view in Bondi: the RSL at the north end. Sign in as a guest, head up to the wrap-around glass balcony and you get the same knockout beach outlook at a fraction of the price. Sunset here with the surfers still out is hard to beat. Sign-in and hours can vary, so glance at the North Bondi RSL site before you head over.

Bondi faces east, so the sun sets behind you over the rooftops, not the sea. The magic light is actually the glow ON the water and the headlands — aim to have a drink in hand by about 30 minutes before sunset and watch the whole beach turn gold.
Craft beer, cocktails and cosy corners
4. Curly Lewis Brewing Co.

Bondi's own microbrewery, tucked just back from Campbell Parade, brews everything on-site — the tanks are right there behind the bar. I come for a tasting paddle to work out my mood before committing to a pint, usually landing on whatever hazy pale they've got pouring. Communal tables, an easy beer-garden feel, and the sort of place where a quick one turns into three.
5. The Anchor

A small, buzzy cocktail spot on Campbell Parade that locals took to quickly. It's tight, it's loud in the best way, and the drinks list rewards a bit of adventurousness — good for kicking off a night rather than settling in for hours. Get there earlier on weekends if you want a seat.
6. Beach Road Hotel

A couple of streets back on Beach Road, this big multi-level pub is the reliable all-rounder — cold schooners, pub classics on the plate, live sport, and DJs and bands upstairs on weekends. It's where a lot of Bondi nights quietly end up. Check their site for what's on before you commit your evening to the top floor.
The rest of my ten
These four round out the list — different moods for different nights:

items: The Bucket List — the sprawling open-air bar right in the Bondi Pavilion, feet-in-the-sand spritzes and one of the best spots for an afternoon session in summer.
Bondi Pavilion Front Yard Bar — the heritage pavilion's casual outdoor bar, festoon lights and a relaxed post-swim crowd.
The Shop (Curlewis Street) — café by day, snug little wine bar by night; my pick for a quiet drink and a cheese plate away from the crowds.
The Beaver — an unpretentious, good-fun bar for burgers, mezcal and a night that doesn't take itself too seriously.

blocks.title: Summer weekends fill fast
blocks.text: From roughly December through February the beachfront venues can hit capacity by mid-afternoon on a hot day. If a table matters — especially at Icebergs or for a big group — book ahead through the venue's own website, and always confirm current opening hours there, as they shift with the season.
How I'd string them together

stops.detail: Finish where the DJs are for a proper late one.

items.q: Which Bondi bar has the best beach view?
items.a: For the postcard shot, the balcony bar at Icebergs above the ocean pool is unbeatable. For the same beach outlook at a much lower price, the upstairs balcony at North Bondi RSL is my go-to. Hotel Ravesis' front terrace is the pick if you want the view with a livelier crowd.

items.q: Where can I drink late in Bondi?
items.a: Hotel Ravesis and the Beach Road Hotel are the two that reliably keep going into the night on weekends, with DJs upstairs. Closing times vary by night and season, so check each venue's own website for current hours.

items.q: Is there craft beer brewed in Bondi?
items.a: Yes — Curly Lewis Brewing Co. is Bondi's own microbrewery, brewing on-site just back from Campbell Parade. A tasting paddle is the best way to find your favourite before committing to a pint.

items.q: How do I get to Bondi Beach for a night out?
items.a: The easiest route from the city is the 333 or 380 bus to Bondi Beach, or catch the train to Bondi Junction and change to a beach-bound bus. Check Transport for NSW for current timetables, and plan your trip home before the last service if you're not grabbing a rideshare.

items.q: Do I need to book ahead?
items.a: For most pubs and casual bars you can just turn up. For Icebergs, or for larger groups on summer weekends, book directly through the venue's website — the beachfront spots fill quickly on hot days.

blocks.text: That's my ten — enough range to build any kind of Bondi night, from a quiet wine after the beach to a full sunset-to-late crawl. Hours, session times and prices do move around with the seasons, so treat this as the shortlist and confirm the details on each venue's own site. Then grab a spot facing the water, get a drink in hand before the light goes, and enjoy the best hour in Bondi.
